assertion.description: The originally described and OMIM-defining presentation: a 46,XY individual with a completely female phenotype — normal female external genitalia, a uterus, and histologically normal ovarian tissue rather than streak gonads. assertion.display_name: CBX2.2 (isoform 2) related, undervirilized phenotype with dysgenetic testes

assertion.name: DiGeorge

genes.description: Bound as the dosage-sensitive gene whose loss drives the thymic/parathyroid/conotruncal arm of this presentation, and the gene in which the cited report found point mutations reproducing it in patients with no 22q11.2 deletion. That report screened TBX1 and does not establish that no other interval gene behaves the same way. In nearly every patient the lesion is the deletion, not a TBX1 sequence variant; see the "Recurrent 22q11.2 deletion" record in `genetic`.

assertion.description: The historical label for the thymic, parathyroid and conotruncal presentation of the 22q11.2 deletion. It is carried here as a named clinical presentation rather than a separate mechanism: the lesion is the same contiguous-gene deletion this entry curates, and the entry already models the immunodeficiency and cardiac arms as pathophysiology nodes. This row exists so that the MONDO concept, and the gene MONDO attaches to it, are addressable in the same place as the presentation they describe.

selected_evidence.snippet: We identified three mutations of TBX1 in two unrelated patients without the 22q11.2 deletion-one with sporadic conotruncal anomaly face syndrome/velocardiofacial syndrome and one with sporadic DiGeorge's syndrome-and in three patients from a family with conotruncal anomaly face syndrome/velocardiofacial syndrome.

assertion.name: Velocardiofacial

genes.description: Bound for the same reason as on the DiGeorge row: TBX1 point mutations without a deletion have been reported in patients with this presentation.

assertion.description: The historical Shprintzen label, emphasising the velopharyngeal, cardiac and facial features. As with DiGeorge syndrome it names a presentation of the same deletion rather than a distinct lesion, and the entry models its mechanistic substrate as the "Velopharyngeal structural and myogenic insufficiency" node. This entry's own description records both, along with CATCH22, as historical labels for the same deletion, which is why the entry is anchored on the deletion and carries them as subtypes rather than splitting into separate disease files.

selected_evidence.snippet: We identified three mutations of TBX1 in two unrelated patients without the 22q11.2 deletion-one with sporadic conotruncal anomaly face syndrome/velocardiofacial syndrome and one with sporadic DiGeorge's syndrome-and in three patients from a family with conotruncal anomaly face syndrome/velocardiofacial syndrome.

selected_evidence.snippet: We also identified affected individuals in two apparently dominant families, diagnosed with juvenile retinitis pigmentosa or dominant cone-rod dystrophy, respectively, who are heterozygous for a 12-bp AIPL1 deletion.

selected_evidence.snippet: The phenotype of LCA in patients with AIPL1 mutations is relatively severe, with a maculopathy in most patients and keratoconus and cataract in a large subset.

assertion.name: Classic Achromatopsia
assertion.description: The majority ATF6-related phenotype: complete or near-complete cone dysfunction from birth with foveal hypoplasia, corresponding to achromatopsia type 7 (ACHM7) in the achromatopsia gene series.

selected_evidence.snippet: Patients had evidence of foveal hypoplasia and disruption of the cone photoreceptor layer.

assertion.name: Cone-Rod Dystrophy
assertion.description: A minority phenotype in which cone responses are extinguished but rod responses are also decreased, with some residual color discrimination -- clinically distinct from classic achromatopsia despite the shared genetic cause. No ATF6-specific numbered cone-rod dystrophy entry exists in OMIM/MONDO (ATF6's only disease-specific identifier is achromatopsia 7/ACHM7); this subtype is therefore bound to the generic cone-rod dystrophy disease-series term rather than a gene-specific one.

selected_evidence.snippet: Detailed phenotypic examination revealed extinguished cone responses but also decreased rod responses together with the ability to discriminate some colours suggestive rather for cone-rod dystrophy than achromatopsia.
